title: Friend charged us for her birthday dinner
author: Storytime
hook: My friend invited six of us to her birthday dinner. At the end, she sent everyone a payment request for a hundred and forty dollars.
story: My friend Bianca turned thirty last Saturday. She booked a fancy steakhouse and invited six of us. Halfway through dessert, our phones buzzed at the same time. A payment request from Bianca. One hundred forty dollars each. Note, my birthday dinner, love you! We had all ordered pretty cheap. Salads, one drink. But okay, it's her birthday. We paid. On the way out, I went back to get my scarf. The manager was clearing our table. He smiled and said, tell Bianca thanks again for the post. I asked, what post? He said, she's one of our partner creators. Her table is always free, as long as she posts a video. Free. The entire dinner. She charged six people a hundred forty dollars for a meal that cost her nothing. That's eight hundred and forty dollars. I checked her page that night. The video was up. Birthday dinner with my besties, hashtag ad. We were in it. Smiling. Holding the glasses we paid for. The group chat doesn't know yet. Should I tell them?
caption: the dinner was free. for HER 💸 #storytime
sound: a sly, tense jazz bass line at very low volume
why: Hosts charging guests is a trending dinner drama, the cheap salads set up the outrage, the free partner table is a satisfying twist, and should I tell them splits the comments.

title: My ex-husband's new girlfriend
author: Storytime
hook: Every Sunday, my ex-husband and I have lunch with our kids. Last week, he brought his new girlfriend. My daughter recognized her.
story: My ex-husband Tom and I divorced three years ago. It wasn't dramatic. We just grew apart. We agreed on one rule. Every Sunday, lunch together with the kids. No matter what. Last week, Tom texted, is it okay if I bring someone? I said sure. I'll be honest, I was nervous. I'd spent the whole morning picking an outfit, which is ridiculous. She walked in. Tall, curly hair, kind smile. Her name was Rachel. Before she even sat down, my nine year old daughter, Lily, stood up and said, it's you. I was confused. Lily said, you're the lady from the park. Four years ago, Lily choked on a grape at a playground. I was on the phone with work, twenty feet away. A woman ran over, did the Heimlich, and saved her. By the time I got there, the woman was gone. I never got her name. I've thought about her every single day. It was Rachel. She had no idea Lily was Tom's daughter. She just remembered a little girl in a yellow raincoat. I couldn't stop crying. Tom couldn't either. So, how do you thank someone for saving your child's life?
caption: she saved my daughter four years ago 💛 #storytime
sound: a gentle, emotional piano that swells softly at very low volume
why: Co-parenting and ex stories are trending, viewers expect jealousy drama, the park rescue twist is deeply emotional, and the thank you question invites heartfelt comments.

title: I was number seven on her spreadsheet
author: Storytime
hook: On our third date, she showed me her spreadsheet ranking every first date she'd been on this year. I was number seven. Number one was my brother.
story: I met Sophie on a dating app. Funny, smart, totally my type. On our third date, she was showing me photos on her laptop, and a spreadsheet popped up. It was titled, first dates, twenty twenty six. She laughed and said, okay, don't judge me. It had columns. Name. Date. Conversation score. Red flags. Green flags. Overall. Twenty-three guys. I was number seven. My red flag column said, too polite, might be hiding something. My green flag said, good laugh, asked about my mom. Fair. Honestly, I was kind of flattered to make the top ten out of twenty-three. Then I looked at number one. Overall score, ten out of ten. Green flags, funny, honest, perfect first date. Red flags, none. The name was Ryan. My brother. She saw my face and asked what's wrong. I said, number one is my brother. She went white. Her hands were literally shaking. She said, he never called me back. I said, he got engaged two weeks after your date. Sophie closed the laptop very slowly. Then she said, okay. But you're still in the top ten. And honestly, I laughed so hard the waiter came over to check on us. Should I go on a fourth date?
caption: I lost to my own brother 📊 #storytime
sound: an awkward, comedic piano with a playful bounce at very low volume
why: Dating storytime stays at the top of the genre, the spreadsheet is a funny visual hook, the brother reveal is absurd, and the fourth date question gets lots of joke comments.
